interest: Shows 1935 Costa Rica blocking a Yokohama Specie Bank branch and curbing Japanese imports amid consumer boycotts.
overview: Despatch No. 857 (Sept. 1935): Minister Sack reports Costa Rica's Foreign Minister Gurdián denied rumors of a Yokohama Specie Bank branch in San José and vowed to restrict Japanese imports, amid growing anti-Japanese sentiment prompting merchants to hide 'Made in Japan' labels.

people.name: Raúl Gurdián
people.role: Minister for Foreign Affairs of Costa Rica

subfiles.about: Report on rumors of the Yokohama Specie Bank opening a branch in San José and the Costa Rican government's refusal to permit Japanese banking expansion.
subfiles.from: Leo R. Sack (U.S. Minister to Costa Rica)
subfiles.summary: Minister Sack reports Costa Rica's Gurdián denied rumors of a Yokohama Specie Bank branch in San José, vowing no authorization and continued curbs on Japanese imports, while merchants hid 'Made in Japan' markings amid rising consumer opposition.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 857 from Leo R. Sack on Rumored Yokohama Specie Bank Branch in San José
